name: payments
title: Payments
summary: Charging customers through provider adapters (card, digital wallet): payment intents per checkout attempt, authorization and capture per order and seller group, declines with retry, uncertain results resolved by a status-check job, refund execution (Requested → Processing → Sent / Failed) capped at the remaining refundable amount, chargebacks and payment disputes, saved payment methods and provider webhooks.
owns: Payment intents: one per checkout payment attempt, with tender split (card or wallet, plus store credit in phase 3), method snapshot and allocation to seller groups
Authorization, capture (on acceptance, or per seller group on dispatch) and voids
Declines with a customer-safe reason and retry with the same or another method; the cart and order reference are kept by checkout
Uncertain results (timeouts, provider errors): pending check with a status-check job, never a second charge
Orphan detection: money authorized or captured without an order is voided or refunded

Refund execution for full orders, selected items and partial amounts: cap at the remaining refundable amount per item, duplicate prevention, destination and timing, Requested → Processing → Sent / Failed with provider-checked retries
Chargebacks and payment disputes queue with evidence deadlines
Saved payment methods: tokenized at the provider, label, brand, last 4 and expiry, default, removable without affecting receipts
notOwns: Refund requests and their approval (Requested, Under review, Approved): returns; payments starts at hand-over
Cancellation decisions and refund amounts for cancellations: orders
Seller balances, holds for chargebacks, fee reversals and the daily reconciliation (payments vs orders, provider deposits): finance
Store credit balances and holds: wallet (phase 3)
Checkout steps, idempotent order placement and the payment-result page flow: checkout

stateMachines.name: Payment intent
stateMachines.notes: Customer view: Accepted = authorized, partially_captured or captured; Pending = authorizing, requires_action or pending_check; Failed = failed, voided before an order or expired. Refunded and Partly refunded are derived from refunds. A retry after failed is a new intent (attempt n+1) for the same checkout session; only one non-failed intent per session can exist, so a double submit cannot authorize twice. pending_check is resolved only by asking the provider (job or webhook), never by charging again. reduce lowers the authorized amount through the adapter's partial reversal (ProviderCall partial_void) when items are cancelled before capture and the adapter supports it; without support the authorized amount stays and the cancelled card share is only taken off the allocations (released at the final capture by close_remainder). An intent paid entirely by store credit (card share 0) goes authorized → captured on capture with no provider call.

stateMachines.name: Refund execution
stateMachines.notes: Starts when returns hands over an approved refund request, orders cancels items, finance records a correction or payments finds an orphan payment. Approval (Under review, Approved) lives in returns. processing covers provider-pending and unknown outcomes (outcomeUnknown); retry first retrieves the provider's record of the earlier attempt and only resends when the provider confirms nothing was sent, so a refund is never sent twice. Each attempt stores its provider idempotency key (refunds.attempt_key) before the provider call, so a status check or retry after a restart asks about the same attempt. Retries stop at refundMaxAttempts; then the customer is asked for a new destination or support takes over. A new destination chosen by the customer (saved method or single-use token) is stored on the refund (refunds.destination_ref) before it is sent, so an uncertain send is checked and retried to the same destination after a restart; it is cleared when the refund is sent or cancelled. Store credit destinations (phase 3) go through wallet.creditRefund and are sent immediately. cancel requires a reason (e.g. settled another way) and releases the in-flight amount.

stateMachines.name: Payment dispute
stateMachines.notes: The provider takes the money back when a chargeback opens; finance holds the seller amount on payments.chargeback.opened and applies or releases it on payments.chargeback.decided. accept (concede) is audited and needs approval above the staff member's limit. Inquiries that close without a chargeback end as won.

consumes.name: orders.order.placed
consumes.does: Link the intent to the order and store seller-group allocations (fallback when linkOrder was not called)

consumes.name: orders.order.accepted
consumes.does: Capture the authorization when captureMode is on_acceptance: the card is charged only the card share; the store-credit share is taken from the wallet hold and reported as creditAmount (a credit-only order is captured with amount 0)

consumes.name: shipping.shipment.dispatched
consumes.does: Capture the group's allocation when captureMode is per_group_on_dispatch: the card is charged only the group's card share (allocation minus its store-credit share, reported as creditAmount; a group paid entirely by credit is captured with amount 0)

consumes.name: orders.order.cancelled
consumes.does: Void the authorization if nothing was captured, and return the uncaptured store-credit share to the wallet

consumes.name: orders.item.cancelled
consumes.does: Start a cancellation refund for the item's refund breakdown (origin cancellation, originId = the event's cancellationId, no Finance approval; one cancellation of several items publishes one event per item, so each item gets its own refund keyed by cancellationId + itemId and the (origin, origin_id) uniqueness does not apply to cancellations; the part above the item's remaining amount, such as the shipping of items cancelled earlier refunded when the last part of a package is cancelled, comes from the package's other items, smallest remaining first) or reduce the uncaptured authorization (partial reversal through the adapter when supported). Before capture, the item's store-credit share goes back to the wallet (wallet.creditRefund, keyed by the item) and only its card share is taken off the authorization; an authorization whose remaining card amount drops to 0 is voided (payments.payment.voided) instead of being left to lapse

consumes.name: access.approval.decided
consumes.does: Complete or drop a dispute concession waiting for approval; carry out an approved manual money action (payments.payments.correct: capture, void, orphan refund, refund retry or cancel) with what was asked, as the approver

jobs.name: payments.check-uncertain
jobs.does: Retrieve pending_check intents from the provider with backoff (30 s, 1 min, 2 min, 5 min…); while an intent with a store-credit hold is pending, keep the hold alive with wallet.extendHold (until the next check plus a margin) so it never lapses into INSUFFICIENT_CREDIT; after uncertainMaxHours raise it to Finance (payments.payment.orphaned with needs_review if money moved)

jobs.name: payments.process-refunds
jobs.does: Submit requested refunds; retrieve processing refunds with unknown outcome; retry failed refunds with retryable reasons up to refundMaxAttempts after confirming with the provider that nothing was sent

jobs.name: payments.detect-orphans
jobs.does: Intents authorized or captured with no order after orphanGraceMinutes and a completed or expired checkout session: void authorizations, start refunds for captures, publish payments.payment.orphaned

jobs.name: payments.expire-authorizations
jobs.does: Walks every live authorization (authorized or partially_captured) in keyset pages ordered by (updated_at, id) until none are left, never only the oldest page: an authorization with no card amount left is voided at once (groups paid entirely by store credit count as charged, never as open card amount); authorizations near expiry are captured if the order is accepted, otherwise voided. A failed expiry capture is retried on the next run with a new capture key (intent id + expiry + attempt number), never blocked by the failed row's key; one failing intent never stops the walk

jobs.name: payments.dispute-deadlines
jobs.does: Flag disputes with evidence due within 48 h; mark lost when the deadline passed without evidence

jobs.name: payments.card-expiry
jobs.does: Mark saved cards expired; apply provider card-updater results

PAYMENT_METHOD_INVALID.meaning: The token or saved method cannot be used (not found, removed, wrong owner).

PAYMENT_METHOD_EXPIRED.meaning: The saved card has expired; update the expiry or use another card.

PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE.meaning: The payment provider did not respond; nothing was charged by this call. Retry later.

CAPTURE_EXCEEDS_AUTHORIZED.meaning: The capture is more than the remaining authorized amount.

REFUND_EXCEEDS_REFUNDABLE.meaning: The refund is more than the remaining refundable amount for an item or the payment. details.items with remaining per item.

DUPLICATE_REFUND.meaning: A refund for the same origin (return, case, exception, correction or orphan payment; for cancellations the same cancellation and item) already exists. details.refundId.

REFUND_RETRY_LIMIT.meaning: The refund reached its maximum attempts; ask the customer for a new destination.

REFUND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.meaning: The provider has not confirmed the earlier attempt; check status before retrying.

EVIDENCE_WINDOW_CLOSED.meaning: The provider's evidence deadline has passed.

WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID.meaning: The provider signature did not verify.

notes: Purchase intents (2026-10-22, departments phase 3): software purchases, food orders and farm orders (paid in full, or the pay-on-delivery deposit) pay outside checkout. They are intents with purpose purchase, no checkout session and no order; the owning module calls authorizePurchase, completeAction, capturePurchase and voidIntent itself and follows payments.purchase.* events. The orphan sweep, capture on orders.order.accepted / shipment dispatch and the payments.payment.* events skip them. Refunds of captured purchases and their bookkeeping in finance are not built yet (software is captured at once and not refundable in the app; food is captured on delivery, so cancelled orders are only voided; farm is captured when the dealer confirms, and a captured farm order is not cancelled in the app).

No duplicate charges (scenario 3): checkout places with an Idempotency-Key; authorize is idempotent per key and allows one non-failed intent per checkout session; provider calls carry their own idempotency keys (intent id + operation); uncertain outcomes are resolved by retrieving from the provider, never by charging again.

Order of events at Place order: authorize (accepted or pending_check) → checkout creates the order (orders.createOrder) → linkOrder with seller-group allocations → orders.order.accepted → capture. A decline creates no order; the customer keeps the cart and delivery choices and can retry with the same or another method (new intent, same checkout session). If an order never appears, detect-orphans voids or refunds the money.

Capture per seller group: allocations record each group's share; with per_group_on_dispatch each group is captured when it ships and cancelled groups are never captured. At launch the default is one capture on acceptance ('charged once, when the order is accepted').

Capture with store credit (mixed tender): each group's allocation is split into a card share and a store-credit share in proportion to the tenders. A capture charges the card only the card share and reports the credit share as creditAmount on payments.payment.captured. When items are cancelled before capture, their credit share goes back to the wallet and their card share comes off the authorization; an authorization whose card amount drops to 0 is voided. Finance's daily check compares card captures plus creditAmount with the order total.

Credit-only captures: when store credit alone pays the order (card share 0) or a seller group (its card share is 0), the capture still happens: payments writes a succeeded capture row with amount 0 and credit_amount, captures the wallet hold share, and publishes payments.payment.captured with amount 0 and creditAmount, keyed like any capture so it happens once. Such groups count as charged everywhere (card amount left, expiry sweep, release of an authorization with nothing left).

Partial reversal (decision D-P1): the provider port has an optional partial reversal (lower an authorization by an amount). When the adapter supports it, cancelling items before capture lowers the authorization by their card share (ProviderCall partial_void, intent transition reduce); when it does not, the authorized amount stays, the card share is tracked in the allocations and the remainder is released at the final capture (close_remainder) or voided when nothing is left.

Refund caps: remaining = paid per item (orders.getPaidAmounts) − sent − in flight (requested, processing and failed: a failed refund keeps reserving its amount until it is sent, retried to a new destination or cancelled; cancelRefund releases it). Every refund names its items, so a partial refund never marks other items refunded. Destination is the original method by default; card refunds show the timing note; a failed card refund asks the customer for a new destination. The credit part of a mixed tender goes back to store credit first (wallet, phase 3).

Approval split: returns approves refund requests (Finance limits from access) and hands them over with startRefund; cancellation refunds follow the cancellation policy and start from orders.item.cancelled; finance starts correction refunds. Payments never shows Approved; its customer states are Requested, Processing, Sent and Failed.
Saved methods: only provider tokens and display data are stored. Removing a method detaches it at the provider; payments keep their MethodSnapshot so receipts and refunds are unaffected.

Daily reconciliation (payments vs orders, provider deposits, unexplained amounts) is finance's ops/finance-checks; finance reads payments.payment.captured, payments.refund.sent and payments.payment.orphaned and corrects through startRefund.

Dependencies: architecture lists orders. Optional: access (dispute concession limits), customers (billing addresses), media (dispute evidence files), wallet (store credit tender and refunds, resolved lazily at call time because wallet depends on payments).

Store credit refunds: payments calls wallet.creditRefund for the refunds it executes with destination store_credit and for the store-credit part of a mixed tender; returns calls it directly for return refunds to store credit, which do not reach payments. Both pass the refund id, so an overlap or retry never credits twice. wallet is phase 3 and an optional dependency resolved at call time; while it is off a store_credit destination is refused.
